clue.text: Added into pop, wine drink recalled mild seasoning

indicators.note: the reversed drink is placed inside the word for father, as if added into it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, as is papa

indicators.note: called back, so the drink's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: kir is white wine mixed with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a fizzy drink and a wine cocktail lead somehow to a gentle spice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop here is father, not a fizzy drink; kir is a French aperitif of white wine and cassis.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a ground red pepper spice, usually milder in heat than cayenne.

clue.text: Not worth having drink that goes up with tax

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the drink's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
to tax someone is to try them, strain their patience

explanation.surface: A grumble about a drink whose price keeps climbing with tax until it is no longer worth buying.
explanation.walkthrough: Tax is a verb here: to try or strain, as in trying one's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paltry is trivial or meagre, too small an amount to be worth bothering about.

clue.text: Supply lines effective in expedition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to feed forgotten lines to an actor
second meaning: quick and punctual, expedition meaning speed

explanation.walkthrough: Supply lines and expedition suggest an army on the march; in fact one is theatre, the other is the old sense of expedition as promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre prompter feeds actors their words, and a prompt reply is one made with speed.

clue.text: One is about following eye movements at the last gasp

indicators.note: the letters for one plus is go around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
next means coming after, following
REM is rapid eye movement, the phase of sleep

explanation.surface: Someone at their final breath, eyes flickering as death approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-plus-is wrapper splits so that a single letter starts the answer and the word is closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in an extreme situation, especially at the point of death.

clue.text: Superior muscle turned to flab at the end

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles; one is an ab

indicators.note: turned round, so the word to plus the final letter are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word flab is used

parts.note: only its final letter is wanted here

explanation.surface: A fitness lament: a once-superior six-pack has finally gone to flab.
explanation.walkthrough: Superior is a noun: the head of a religious house, not an adjective about the muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey of monks, their religious superior.

clue.text: Posh private among soldiers — a considerable number!

parts.note: U is upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: the private soldier sits in among the letters for soldiers

parts.note: men is the usual word for soldiers in the ranks
Pte is the army abbreviation for the rank of private

explanation.surface: An upper-class private serving among ordinary soldiers, of whom there are a great many.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the old U and non-U classification of English speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a large but indefinite quantity.

clue.text: Wearing special clothes designed at Corpus Christi?

parts.note: Corpus Christi is a college at Oxford and at Cambridge, so it stands for a university
formed, shaped or made

explanation.surface: Clothes created by an Oxford or Cambridge college, worn on special occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Corpus Christi is the name of colleges in both Oxford and Cambridge, hinted at by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uniformed means dressed in a uniform, the special outfit of a group or job.

clue.text: Fills out parking notices

parts.note: ads are advertisements, public notices

explanation.surface: A traffic warden filling out parking tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad is to fill out, as with stuffing a cushion or padding an essay.

clue.text: City welcomes MP Tam, possibly one speaking forcefully

indicators.note: the city's letters take the others in, as a host welcomes guests

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
taken as written
a tam is a kind of hat, so possibly signals an example
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A city welcomes a politician called Tam, who turns out to be a forceful orator.
explanation.walkthrough: Tam reads like a man's name (Scots for Tom) but is a tam-o'-shanter, a Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic describes speech delivered with force and conviction, stressing its point.

clue.text: Gas inert — no good for explosion

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry warning: an inert gas is no good if you want an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface calls the gas inert, and the answer is in fact fairly unreactive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless element making up most of the air we breathe.

clue.text: Solo cracking — Coltrane's coda unrestrained

indicators.note: cracking breaks the word solo apart so its letters can be reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
the coda, the closing part, of the name Coltrane is its final letter

explanation.surface: A jazz review: John Coltrane cutting loose in a solo at the end of a number.
explanation.walkthrough: Coda is a musical term for the closing passage, used here for the last letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free from restraint, as an animal running loose.

clue.text: Driving hazard traps learner in two tricky situations

indicators.note: the first tricky situation holds the learner inside it

parts.note: a bind is a tricky situation, a predicament
L is the learner-driver plate
a spot is a tricky situation, as in a tight spot

explanation.surface: A learner driver caught in a couple of awkward moments on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Two tricky situations means two separate words for a predicament, a bind and a spot, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is the area a driver cannot see in the mirrors, a well-known road hazard.

clue.text: On appeal, this may need saying again and again!

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
a petition is a formal appeal or request

explanation.surface: A wry note that any appeal needs to be made over and over to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition is the act of saying or doing something again and again.

clue.text: Just one dropped round in Algarve location

indicators.note: the letter for one is let fall out of the word

parts.note: fair means just, even-handed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A holiday tale of losing a round of drinks somewhere in the Algarve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Algarve is the southern coastal region of Portugal, popular with British holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is the regional capital and airport city of the Algarve in southern Portugal.

clue.text: Mo's meaning — at first — men doubly misinterpreted

definitions.note: read as Mo is: Mo is the chemical symbol of this element

indicators.note: only the first letter of meaning is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is wanted here

indicators.note: read wrongly, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Mo has had their meaning misunderstood twice over by men.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo looks like a person's name but is a chemical symbol; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Molybdenum is the metallic element whose chemical symbol is Mo, used in hard steel alloys.

clue.text: Speak without script in English, needing variable increase in speed?

parts.note: x is the standard algebraic variable
tempo is the speed of a piece of music
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Advice for an English speaker improvising: vary your pace and speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: An increase in speed is a tempo rise, so the speed comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To extemporise is to speak or perform without preparation, improvising as you go.

clue.text: Difficult task from High Command?

parts.note: tall means high
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A tough mission handed down by senior military commanders.
explanation.walkthrough: High Command looks like the military leadership, but read literally it is a tall order.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a request that is unreasonably hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Old black cat protecting four in forgotten state

indicators.note: the big cat wraps around four, sheltering it

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old black cat guarding a litter of four, in a forgotten corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the condition of being forgotten or unaware, sunk out of memory.

clue.text: Additional material transforms liturgical books

parts.note: PS, postscript, is material added after a letter
alters means changes, transforms

explanation.surface: A note that added material changes the church's service books.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books containing the psalms, used in church worship.

clue.text: A quiet man in tree has time to celebrate

indicators.note: the article, quiet and man sit inside the tree

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree
taken as written
still means quiet, silent
Ed, a man's name

explanation.surface: A silent man sitting up a tree, taking time off for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is part of the definition, not the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastille Day, 14 July, is France's national holiday marking the storming of the Paris prison.

clue.text: Socialist craftsman dancing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William ..., Victorian designer and socialist
second meaning: ... dancing, English folk dance

explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is traditional English folk dancing with bells and sticks; William Morris led the Arts and Crafts movement.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris was a textile designer and socialist; the morris is an English folk dance.

clue.text: Cool husband on beer to have inspirational experience?

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A trendy husband drinking beer, hoping for some inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration here is literal: breathing in, its medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to draw air into the lungs, which is inspiration in the breathing sense.

clue.text: Without employment, indulged regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one starting from the first

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of this word are kept

explanation.surface: Out of work and indulging oneself on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working, unoccupied, with no job to do.

clue.text: How peat-cutters might be overwhelmed?

definitions.meaning: peat is dug from bogs, so peat-cutters might literally be down in a bog
the everyday sense: swamped, unable to make progress

explanation.walkthrough: Peat is cut from boggy ground, so the idiom for being stuck is pictured literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck under too much work is an idiom drawn from getting mired in marshy ground.

clue.text: Dynamic people needing energy to move shrub

indicators.note: the energy letter is shifted to a new position within the word for dynamic people

parts.note: goers are energetic, go-ahead people

explanation.surface: Go-getters needing their energy to move a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Needing energy to move says the E of goers shifts, here to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny evergreen bush with yellow flowers, common on heathland.

clue.text: Channel Island one discarding king's dress

indicators.note: the island throws away the letter for king

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Channel Islander throwing away the king's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off Normandy and include Jersey, Guernsey, Alderney and Sark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Northerner, large bounder tucking into cooked rice

indicators.note: the antelope goes inside the cooked rice, like a diner tucking into food
cooked means the letters of rice are prepared in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the eland is a large leaping African antelope

explanation.surface: A big lout from the north tucking into a plate of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder looks like a cad but is literally a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Iceland in the far North Atlantic is a northerner by geography.

clue.text: Woman not completely common

indicators.note: the word for common is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: normal means common, ordinary

explanation.surface: A woman described as not entirely common.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female given name, as in the Bellini opera heroine.

clue.text: More unpleasant wine consumed by emperor endlessly

indicators.note: the wine is swallowed inside the emperor's name
the emperor's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Nero, Roman emperor
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A decadent emperor knocking back wine and growing nastier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, so more disagreeable or unpleasant.

clue.text: Direction needed to hold ceremony all together

indicators.note: the compass direction holds the ceremony within it

parts.note: ENE, east-northeast, is a compass direction
Mass is the Catholic eucharistic ceremony

explanation.surface: Instructions for a ceremony where everyone gathers in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means as a group, everyone at once.
